nodes.name: One-step hydrothermal synthesis of CeO2-x/rGO variants
nodes.procedure: A one-step hydrothermal method was used to prepare CeO2-x on rGO (CeO2-x/rGO) with different densities achieved by controlling various amounts of Ce precursors: (i) low-density nanoparticles (L-CeO2-x/rGO), (ii) medium-density nanoparticles (M-CeO2-x/rGO), and (iii) high-density nanoparticles (H-CeO2-x/rGO). Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) images illustrated that the one-step hydrothermal method achieved the various densities of CeO2-x/rGO.
nodes.source_text: We used a one-step hydrothermal method to prepare CeO2-x on rGO (CeO2-x/rGO). ... Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) images further illustrated that a one-step hydrothermal method achieved the various densities of CeO2-x/rGO (Figure S2).

nodes.name: Pt single atom loading on L-CeO2-x/rGO
nodes.procedure: The electrostatic adsorption mechanism enables the negatively charged PtCl6^2- directed to grow on positively charged L-CeO2-x instead of negatively charged rGO. Then, PtSA is selectively coordinated to the L-CeO2-x surface forming the PtSA-L-CeO2-X/rGO by sintering reduction.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images illustrate various densities of CeO2-x nanoparticles on rGO for L-, M-, and H-CeO2-x/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) images further illustrated that a one-step hydrothermal method achieved the various densities of CeO_{2 - X}/rGO (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: White circles indicate monodispersed PtSA on CeO2-x nanoparticles in PtSA-M-CeO2-x/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM image of Pt_{SA}-M-CeO_{2-X}/rGO. White circles indicate monodispersed Pt_{SA}.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows Pt elements selectively and uniformly dispersed on CeO2-x nanoparticles, not on rGO, with decreasing brightness indicating decreasing Pt density from H to L.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mapping indicated that the Pt elements are selectively and uniformly dispersed on CeO_{2-X} nanoparticles, rather than on rGO (Figure S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes show (222) crystal plane of CeO2-x particles exposed; SAED indicates (844) and (044) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The oxygen-deficient structure of CeO_{2-X} is further identified by measuring the lattice fringes of Pt_{SA}-CeO_{2-X}/rGO, which shows that (222) is the exposed crystal plane of CeO_{2-X} particles (Figure S10a).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS k³χ(k) Fourier transform spectra of Pt in R-space show Pt-O bond at 1.63 Å for all catalysts; Pt/CeO2 shows Pt-Pt bond at 2.27 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The major peak around 1.63Å corresponds to the Pt-O bond, indicating that the Pt coordinates with the O in CeO_{2-X} to form Pt_{SA}... The peaks of Pt/CeO2 at R = 1.44Å and 2.27Å correspond to the Pt-O and Pt-Pt bond, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2-x content increases from 17.6 wt% (L) to 27.6 wt% (M), 32.4 wt% (H); PtSA remains at 0.8 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) tests confirm that the content of CeO_{2-X} in X-CeO_{2-X}/rGO gradually increased from 17.6 wt% (X = L) to 27.6 wt% (X = M), 32.4 wt% (X = H).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Pt 4f spectra of PtSA-M-CeO2-x/rGO resolved into Pt⁰ and Pt²⁺ components.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution XPS spectra of Pt 4f for Pt_{SA}-M-CeO_{2-x}/rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Absence of Pt peaks due to low Pt content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectrum (Figure S13) indicates that the absence of Pt peaks in the XRD spectrum may be due to the low content of Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge XANES of PtSA-M-CeO2-x/rGO shows Pt oxidation state of +0.35.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The oxidation state of Pt in Pt_{SA}-M-CeO_{2-X}/rGO and Pt/CeO_2 was estimated to be +0.35 and +0.39, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectra show signal at g=2.003 confirming oxygen vacancies in CeO2-x/rGO and PtSA-M-CeO2-x/rGO; PtSA addition increases surface defect centers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CeO_{2-X}/rGO and Pt_{SA}-M-CeO_{2-X}/rGO present an evident signal with a g value of 2.003, suggesting that CeO_{2-X} contains oxygen vacancies... The EPR curves of Pt_{SA}-CeO_{2-X}/rGO have a slightly higher peak area than that of the CeO_{2-X}/rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform maximum intensity at k=2.5 Å⁻¹ agrees with PtO2, confirming Pt-O bond formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The maximum intensity of Pt_{SA}-M-CeO_{2-X}/rGO occurs at k = 2.5Å^{-1} in agreement with that of PtO_2, suggesting a Pt-O bond formation.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtSA loading has negligible impact on morphology of CeO2-x/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) images of X-CeO_{2-X}/rGO and Pt_{SA}-X-CeO_{2-X}/rGO show that the loading of Pt_{SA} has a negligible impact on the morphology.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern indicates CeO2-x exposes (844) and (044) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern indicates that CeO_{2-X} exposes the (844) and (044) planes (Figure S10b).
